title: Notebooks and mockups — the workflow transfers
intro: The finale swaps codebases for other artifacts: a messy EDA notebook, then a Figma design file.

steps.title: The notebook refactor
steps.body:
One structured prompt on `@EDA.ipynb`: keep the analysis and graphs, then —

- **Inventory first**: what metrics, visualizations, transformations, quality issues exist.
- **Structure**: named sections (objectives → loading → preparation → metrics → summary), a table of contents, a data dictionary of business terms.
- **Extraction**: `business_metrics.py` and `data_loader.py` as reusable modules with docstrings.
- **Visual bar**: every plot gets a descriptive title and labeled axes with units.

steps.title: Then a dashboard
steps.body: With clean modules extracted, the dashboard request builds on tested parts instead of notebook cells — the refactor wasn't cosmetic, it was preparation.

steps.title: Figma to running app
steps.body: Lesson 8: `npx create-next-app@latest .`, then attach **two MCP servers** — Figma Dev-Mode (enabled in the desktop app, `claude mcp add --transport http figma-dev-mode-mcp-server http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`) and Playwright — verified with `/mcp`.

points.label: Source of truth
points.note: The Figma MCP server lets Claude READ the mockup — components, layout, styles — instead of guessing from a description.

points.label: Builder
points.note: One prompt: analyze the mockup, build it in this Next.js app with recharts.

points.label: Verifier
points.note: Playwright: 'check how this application looks and verify it matches the mock as closely as possible.' Claude compares its own output against the design.

points.label: Real data
points.note: Follow-up: 'populate these charts with real-world data from FRED' — the mockup becomes a live dashboard.

steps.title: Nothing new — that's the point
steps.body: Inventory-first is lesson 2's exploration. Verify-with-Playwright is lesson 3's loop. Structured demands are lesson 4's template. The finale's lesson is **transfer**: notebooks, dashboards and design files are all just codebases with different file extensions.

recap:
**Same discipline, new media.**

- Notebooks: inventory → structure → extraction → visual bar, then the dashboard.
- Figma: one MCP server reads the truth, another verifies the result.
- Claude builds AND checks — against artifacts, not adjectives.
- The workflow transfers to any artifact you can address.
